the next-to-next-leading order corrections in supersymmetric theories are very similar to those of the Standard Model, but that in the case of light top squarks a deviation of the order of 10% can be expected.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of higher-order corrections for a light Higgs boson in supersymmetric QCD.
the evaluation of the next-to-nextto-leading order corrections in the production of a Higgs boson in gluon gluon fusion.
the computation of the next-to-nextto-leading order cross section for gluon fusion in a large part of parameter space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the next-to-next to leading order corrections to Higg boson production in the gluon fusion process are very important for the precise prediction of the cross sections in the supersymmetric theory and the Standard Model, but that their effect on the cross section ratio is small.
the supersymmetric next-to-next-leading order corrections are not large and that the supersymmetric scenario is still viable.
the supersymmetric theory can be considered as a very competitive theory in view of the recent discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the next-to-next-leading order corrections are not able to distinguish a supersymmetric theory from the Standard Model in the light top squark scenario, where the supersymmetric theory has a light Higgs boson with a mass of 125 GeV.

supersymmetric QCD effects can be neglected in a first step in the analysis of the Higgs boson data at the LHC, while the next-to-next-leading order corrections are of the order of a few per mille and should be included in the analysis.
the supersymmetric QCD corrections to the production of a Higgs boson with a mass of about 125GeV are not very different from the ones of the Standard Model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of the new higher-order terms in the calculation of the cross section does not alter our understanding of the Higgs sector in supersymmetry.
the next-to-next-leading order corrections to gluon fusion Higgs boson cross section are rather small and that the Standard Model and the MSSM are very similar in this respect.
